headline: LLMs embedded in agentic retrieval and reasoning pipelines over biomedical sources
label: Llm Systems For Biomedical Literature
summary: Early 2026 papers report multi-step LLM pipelines over curated databases and literature for genomics and biomedical QA.
synthesis: The dominant thread is LLMs coupled to external biomedical sources through retrieval, agent orchestration, or federated knowledge access, rather than used as standalone responders. GenomAgent coordinates specialized agents over databases and reports a 12% average gain over GeneGPT. MedHopper pairs an agentic RAG-LLM with a bounded state machine and reranking, scoring 0.55 EM on MedHopQA. RAGulate grounds TF-target regulatory assessment in CollecTRI and PubMed evidence, and BTE-RAG draws on a federated API of over sixty biomedical knowledge sources. SciHorizon-GENE provides a gene-to-function benchmark of over 540K questions drawn from curated databases. I-NOWJ addresses a narrower extraction problem, Spanish clinical substance-use NER, using knowledge-guided augmentation and adaptive context selection. New elements are explicit agent orchestration, bounded state, and adaptive context selection. Reported metrics span different tasks and are not directly comparable.
